concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of acute hypogastric pain and nausea, combined with the radiographic findings of an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, and small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right, are consistent with intussusception.

The patient's symptoms of acute hypogastric pain and nausea, combined with the radiographic findings of an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, and small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right, are also consistent with volvulus.

The patient's symptoms of acute hypogastric pain and nausea, combined with the physical examination findings of localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium, and positive McBurney's sign, are consistent with appendicitis, although the appendix appeared normal on imaging.
The patient's symptoms of acute hypogastric pain and nausea, combined with the laboratory finding of an elevated white-cell count, are consistent with diverticulitis.

The patient's symptoms of acute hypogastric pain and nausea, combined with the radiographic findings of an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, and small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right, are consistent with mesenteric ischemia, although there were no signs of ischemia on imaging.

The patient's symptoms of acute hypogastric pain and nausea, combined with the physical examination findings of localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium, are consistent with ovarian torsion, although the pelvic ultrasonography was negative for gynecological pathology.

The patient's symptoms of occasional postprandial abdominal discomfort and acute hypogastric pain are consistent with abdominal wall pain, although the physical examination findings and laboratory results suggest a more serious underlying condition.

The patient's symptoms of acute hypogastric pain and nausea, combined with the radiographic findings of an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, and small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right, are consistent with intestinal adhesions.
The abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and the appendix appearing normal suggest malrotation of the intestine.

rationales.F06: McBurney's sign is highly suggestive of appendicitis.
rationales.F09: Abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure is consistent with malrotation of the intestine.
rationales.F11: Abnormal superior mesenteric artery-vein relationship is consistent with malrotation of the intestine.
rationales.F12: Normal appearance of the appendix makes appendicitis less likely.
